prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
competitors_mentioned: Colorado Division of Professions and Occupations
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name a single universal “best” roofer for hail damage — the right contractor depends on your exact location, the size/type of roof, whether you need an emergency patch or full replacement, and whether you’re going through insurance. I can, however, help you find a highly qualified roofer and give concrete steps and questions so you can pick the best option in Denver.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and whether this is an emergency (active leak) or an insurance claim — I’ll give a short list of well-reviewed local roofers and/or next steps. Meanwhile, use the checklist below.

What to look for in a hail-damage roofer
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed ShingleMaster). These matter for warranty and installation quality.  
- Experience with insurance claims and hail-specific repairs. Ask how many hail claims they handle annually.  
- Local, permanent office and local references (storm “chasers” are a red flag).  
- Proper licensing, bonded status and current general liability and workers’ comp insurance — verify certificates.  
- Written, itemized estimate and a clear workmanship warranty (length and what it covers) plus manufacturer shingle warranty.  
- Will obtain required permits and coordinate final inspection.  
- Provides photos and a clear plan (replace vs. spot-repair) and a timeline.

Questions to ask every roofer
- Are you licensed and insured in Colorado? Can you show certificates?  
- Do you have GAF/Owens Corning/CertainTeed certification? Which ones?  
- How many local hail repairs have you done in the last 12 months? Can you provide recent references?  
- Do you handle the insurance paperwork and meet with adjusters?  
- What is included/excluded in the estimate? Any sub‑contractors?  
- What warranties do you provide (labor and materials)? How long?  
- Do you offer a storm-damage deductible assistance program? (If they say yes, get details — be wary of offers that waive your deductible in suspicious ways.)

How to avoid scams and bad contractors
- Don’t hire anyone who knocks door-to-door after a storm without verifying credentials.  
- Avoid contractors who demand full payment up front. Use a reasonable payment schedule tied to milestones.  
- Check BBB, Google Reviews, Yelp and the Colorado Division of Professions and Occupations for complaints.  
- Require lien releases from the contractor/subcontractors when you make final payment.

Cost and insurance tips
- Typical full residential roof replacements in the Denver area often run in the low five-figures, depending on size, materials and complexity. Minor hail repairs can be a few hundred to a few thousand dollars. Get three bids.  
- Notify your insurer first and document all damage with photos. A reputable roofer will help prepare estimates and meet the adjuster.  
- If you disagree with the insurer’s settlement, consider a public adjuster or a second opinion from another certified roofer.

If you want local recommendations
- Tell me your ZIP code and whether you’re filing an insurance claim or need emergency work. I’ll give 3–5 well-reviewed Denver-area roofers and prioritize those with hail/insurance experience.
